headline: Profit surges on NAND pricing and datacenter demand
summary_short: Sandisk's fiscal Q4 (quarter ended July 3, 2026) revenue jumped to $8,965M, up 51% q/q and 372% y/y, as NAND pricing and datacenter demand surged, driving GAAP diluted EPS to $43.97 from a $0.16 per-share loss a year ago.
summary_long: Sequential revenue growth was roughly one-third higher volumes and two-thirds higher pricing; the full fiscal year's growth was driven by mix shift toward higher-value customers (Datacenter revenue +437% y/y) plus pricing. Gross margin expanded to 84.6% from 78.4% q/q and 26.2% a year ago on the NAND pricing recovery, while operating expenses were roughly flat q/q ($545M vs $551M), driving the EPS jump. The board expanded its buyback authorization by $14B to $15.5B remaining, and repurchased $4,524M of stock this quarter; free cash flow was $7,083M. For fiscal Q1 2027, Sandisk guides revenue to $10.30B-$10.80B and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $44.00-$46.00.
